title: Boundary edges of odd-dimensional majority
statement: Let $m$ be a natural number, choose a coordinate $i$ among $2m+1$ coordinates, and let $e$ be a cube point whose $i$th coordinate is $1$. The majority function on the $(2m+1)$-dimensional cube changes value across the edge at $e$ in coordinate $i$ if and only if, among the other $2m$ coordinates, exactly $m$ are equal to $1$.
hypotheses_covered: $e$ is a cube point with $i$th coordinate equal to $1
